note: Observability registry: every time the foundation layer gains the ability to OBSERVE something it could not observe before, the existing evidence chain is re-read against it. This file is the record of that re-read, and `project/gates.py observability` keeps it honest.
rule: An upgrade must say which claim rows it re-opened and what the verdict was for each.
A verdict of `promoted` requires README to say L3 for that header; `still_short` requires L2 and a named missing leg.

An implementation-level leg may NOT promote anything. Re-implementing the same rule in another language proves the code does what the code says; it says nothing about whether the rule is right, and L3 in this repository means a cross-model check.
An upgrade that re-opened nothing must say why (`no_effect`), so the next reader can tell 'considered and rejected' from 'never considered'.
known_limit: The mechanical trigger is the evidence string: an L2 row whose evidence names a `test_sil_*` case must be registered. That is a proxy for 'measured on a plant trajectory', and it misses rows measured on the plant through a file without SIL in the name -- `test_soft_limit.cpp`, `test_friction_comp.cpp`, `test_gear_ratio.cpp` and `test_position_reference.cpp` all build a `PmsmPlant` and none of them is caught automatically. They are registered below by hand, and the gap between the proxy and the truth is stated here rather than papered over.

upgrades.capability: Any plant scenario can be replayed period by period in float64 by an independent solver, because the harness dumps the applied phase voltages alongside the state. Closed-loop included, with no controller re-implemented in Python.
upgrades.source: scipy.integrate DOP853 (adaptive, rtol 1e-12) as the second solver; the right-hand side re-derived from `sil_pmsm_plant.hpp`; machine parameters handed over by the C++ side so the two cannot drift. Audits: per-period replay, energy conservation, kinematics, each proved able to go red by `--selftest`.
upgrades.no_effect: Nothing that is still open. `core/homing.hpp` was re-read here in 2026-10-30 and left short on per-source sensitivity (creep speed, index jitter, timeout); O-26 has since measured all three, so the row's verdict lives there -- an implementation-level leg may not carry a promotion, which is exactly the rule that made this entry hand the row over instead of closing it. The float64 replay introduced here is unchanged and is still the cross-model leg the L3 rows stand on.

upgrades.capability: The plant can now carry a Stribeck dip between breakaway and kinetic friction, so a friction claim can be tested against a published model that the compensator does not implement.
upgrades.source: Stribeck curve / Armstrong-Helouvry, Dupont & Canudas de Wit (1994), seven-parameter friction model. The dip is a published, validated mechanism; the plant reproduces it with one width parameter whose default of 0 degenerates to the previous exact-Coulomb law.

reopened.note: O-1 re-opened this row and could not promote it, correctly: an implementation-level leg is not a cross-model check. What promoted it is O-2, and the claim it now carries is a limitation stated with a formula -- inside a dip of width vs at speed v the residual is (Fs-Fc)*exp(-(v/vs)^2)/kKp, unreachable by a law with no state.

upgrades.capability: The speed estimator's noise gain can be measured on a synthetic angle stream with a known error, so its closed-form statistics become checkable rather than asserted.
upgrades.source: Statistics of a difference operator and of a least-squares slope over the same window (textbook regression variance). An analytic leg, not a second simulator: it is derived, so it catches an implementation that does not do what its documentation says, and it is the leg that found F-42.

reopened.note: O-1 re-opened this row and could not promote it (implementation-level). O-3 promotes it: the closed forms are now measured against the shipped estimator, and the measurement discriminates between them. The row also absorbed a defect the derivation exposed -- the header's least-squares factor was wrong by sqrt(2) (F-42).

upgrades.capability: Every master-side error source of the electronic gear now has a closed form that can be measured on a synthetic master, and the header's stated decode assumption is checked instead of promised.
upgrades.source: Kinematics of a sampled wrapped angle plus the arithmetic of telescoping differences: the quantisation bound |ratio|*q is a property of the decoder, the jitter law v_ref = ratio*delta/dt follows from which quantity is wrong, and the lost-count step follows from the unwrap. Derived, not consulted, but derived from the stated assumption rather than from the implementation.

reopened.note: O-1 re-opened this row and could not promote it (implementation-level). O-4 promotes it, and the pass found two defects on the way: kMaxStepRad had no consumer (F-43), and the flag it now sets was copied into the output before being set. Two of the four predictions were also wrong first and are recorded rather than fitted.

upgrades.capability: The profile's three ceilings have closed-form switch points that can be read off the shipped class one ceiling at a time, and the move's own kinematics give the arrival time independently of the code.
upgrades.source: The algebra of `g*e = sqrt(2*a*e)` and `sqrt(2*a*e) = v` for the landmarks, and the trapezoid planner's `D/v + v/a` for the timing -- the move's kinematics, which the profile never computes and which is a different structure (a phase machine) from this one (a minimum of ceilings plus a rate limiter).

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row and named two missing legs. Both are now supplied. The pass also turned A-40's null result into a condition (`g >= 2a/v`) instead of an absence of explanation, and found one documentation defect (F-44: the stopping-distance law was stated as a property of the axis when it is a property of the command). No code defect: the structure was right, which is worth recording, because a row that always finds a bug is a row whose tests are being written to fit.

upgrades.capability: The soft limit's invariant can be solved, not only checked: the cap's seam is an exact observable with no tolerance, which turns 'is the invariant respected' into 'how much speed does this distance buy' and gives one sensitivity coefficient per error source.
upgrades.source: The quadratic `v^2 + 2*a*tau*v - 2*a*d = 0` solved for `v`; the plant's own stopping distance for the delay-travel law. Neither comes from the code: the code never solves for the seam, it only compares against a ceiling each period.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a sensitivity table and a model-level second source; both are supplied. The hypothesised under-protection -- the margin term is computed from the command, so an axis moving faster than it is being commanded should lose protection -- was tested and does not occur, because the cap has already bounded the speed by the time the command can lie. No code defect; what was missing was the solution of the invariant, which is now in the header.

upgrades.capability: The counting channel's four error sources each have an exact closed form, which is a stronger position than the continuous-angle channels are in: the channel is a sum of integers and one division, so the identities can be checked rather than bounded.
upgrades.source: The arithmetic of a sampled wrapped angle: wrap rate `p*s/(2*pi)`, reconstructed turn length `2*pi*p/p'`, and the residue a once-per-revolution mark must therefore see. Nothing here comes from the code; the code never computes a turn length.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for four source coefficients and a model-level second source; both are supplied. Deriving the turn length turned up a real defect (F-45): the index snap had no plausibility guard, so a spurious pulse moved the origin by up to 3.14 rad silently -- and with the guard in place an integer pole-pair error became detectable, which this row could not claim before.

upgrades.capability: The decimated outer loop's period is now an observed quantity rather than a restatement of the configuration, and its stability boundary is predicted by a z-domain model instead of being tuned.
upgrades.source: The trace channel's own sample stream gives the loop's instants; the z-domain difference equation (`L(z) = [omega_b*T*(z-1) + omega_b*T^2/tau_b]/(z-1)^2`) gives the pole locations. Neither is derived from the code -- the code contains no frequency at all in this path.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a sensitivity to the loop period and a model-level second source; both are supplied. Two things fell out that the row could not claim before: the period is quantised to ticks and may be one tick longer than requested (F-46, documented rather than changed), and the decimation limit is 160x with a derivation rather than a rule of thumb.

upgrades.capability: The polarity test's answer is now a function of the d-axis error with a closed form, and its window is measured rather than assumed -- including the limit that closes it first.
upgrades.source: The projection algebra: two factors of `cos(delta)` on the d-axis volt-seconds and the measurement, with the saliency term common-mode. The code contains no angle dependence at all -- it projects on whatever angle it was handed.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a per-source sensitivity and a model-level second source; both are supplied, and the angle sweep turned up F-47 -- the method's premise was unchecked, and a short settle produced a confident wrong polarity. The unit-test fixture had no winding relaxation at all, which is why every case there had been exercising the degenerate path and getting the right label for the wrong reason.

upgrades.capability: The feedforward's error sources are now a closed form with a number per source, and the machine's own steady-state equation is read back through the PI as an independent check.
upgrades.source: The steady-state voltage equation (`di/dt = 0`) of the plant, and the projection of a command built in one frame into another. Neither is in the feedforward: it never sees the plant, and it never sees an angle error.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a parameter-mismatch table and a model-level second source; both are supplied. No defect in the feedforward itself -- its q-axis term is exact to 0.05 % -- but the pass found that the d axis is confounded by the estimator's angle error at 55.5 % of the term it is meant to measure, which is a boundary the row did not have before.

upgrades.capability: The blend's coefficients are now closed forms measured exactly, and the circle-valued nature of the interpolation is a case rather than a comment.
upgrades.source: The algebra of a convex combination plus the geometry of a circle: `theta_low + w*arc(theta_high, theta_low)`. Neither is in the module -- it computes a weight and adds a product.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a sensitivity across the blend region and a model-level second source; both are supplied, with stub observers so the coefficients are exact rather than plant-noise-limited. No defect: what the pass adds is the statement that a handover moves the angle without moving the speed, which a consumer integrating the speed would get wrong by exactly the disagreement.

upgrades.capability: The carrier's three error sources each have a closed form, and the demodulator's own scale is measured and stated instead of being assumed away.
upgrades.source: The high-frequency admittance of a salient machine: `(V/(2*w))*(1/Lq - 1/Ld)`. The module never computes an admittance -- it multiplies a demodulated current by a gain.

reopened.note: O-1 reopened this row for a per-source table and a model-level second source; the sin(2*dtheta) law and the Rs degradation already had cases, and the table adds the amplitude, saliency and sample-timing coefficients. One measurement corrected a claim I would otherwise have made: `hf_current_a` is 3.601630 times the predicted gain at every amplitude, so the formula is right in shape and the factor is the demodulator's -- asserting equality would have been fitting.

upgrades.capability: Per-decision modified condition/decision coverage of the safety subset, so a condition that no case has ever made false is visible instead of being averaged into a line-coverage number.
upgrades.source: clang 18 `-fcoverage-mcdc` + `llvm-cov show --show-mcdc`: the independence pairs per decision, which is a property of the tests rather than of the physics.
upgrades.no_effect: `core/protection.hpp` was left short here on a model-level second source for the two-fault ranking; O-29 has since supplied the derivation that exists (threshold codes are unordered by measurement, durations must follow, path independence verified), so the row's verdict lives there -- an implementation-level leg may not carry a promotion. `core/sm.hpp` is still short and stays so. `core/sm.hpp` was left short here on 'any measurement at all'; O-34 has since measured it as a graph (7 edges, Fault the only sink, refusals inert by exactly one) and fixed the docstring's omitted abort edges (F-108), so the row's verdict lives there -- an implementation-level leg may not carry a promotion.

upgrades.capability: A third, physically different source for the field itself: an independent magnetostatic FEM on a geometry whose answer is closed-form, so that a lumped parameter in this kernel can later be compared against a number that shares no code, no discretisation and no assumptions with it.
upgrades.source: FEMM 4.2 x64 under Wine on this machine, driven through its Lua entry point; the expected value is a closed form derived here and the discriminating power is proved rather than assumed -- the same geometry solved as `planar` returns +40 to +54 % error where the axisymmetric solve returns -0.3 to -0.1 %.
upgrades.no_effect: Nothing is re-opened, and the reason is now a *category* gap rather than a missing instrument. A geometry with a rotor, a magnet and a saturating stator has been solved (pyleecan's IPMSM_A, 48 slots, 8 poles, 0.75 mm gap, 3.15 mm bridges), and the result matched a numeric prediction written down before the run: the gap-field fundamental came out 0.8503 T against a predicted 0.85 T, giving psi_f = 0.3858 Wb-turns against a pre-registered band of 0.35-0.40. That is a stronger validation than the two closed-form cases, because the number was registered in advance and the model had to saturate its way there. It still re-opens no claim row: the rows naming ld/lq/psi_f describe *this* kernel's machine, which has no geometry anywhere in the repository, and a second machine's numbers are not a cross-check of the first -- treating them as one would be the exact self-deception this leg exists to prevent. The gap closes by a decision, not by more code: either give the kernel's own machine a geometry, or declare the reference design explicitly and rewrite the claim rows to name it. Until one of those happens, this leg produces instrument credibility, not claim credibility. (A silent-failure defect was found on the way -- a B-H curve attached before its material existed is discarded with no message, so earlier 'saturating' runs had all been linear. Recorded as F-81; the diff-against-a-known-baseline habit is what caught it.)

upgrades.capability: A measurement of the same physical machine by somebody else. Not another of our own calculations: a number produced on real hardware by a third party, transcribed from a public report with a DOI, which a reader can re-download and re-derive without asking anyone for a datasheet.
upgrades.source: U.S. DOE / Oak Ridge National Laboratory benchmark testing of the 2004 Toyota Prius traction motor -- ORNL/TM-2006/423 (doi:10.2172/947571) Table 3.4, Table 6.2 and Table 6.3, and ORNL/TM-2004/137 (doi:10.2172/885676). Both are OSTI full text. `IPMSM_A` in this repository *is* that machine, so the measurement is of the object the geometry describes. Transcription and unit interpretation are gated by four assertions that must all hold before a comparison is printed, and `oracle_ornl.py --selftest` detunes psi_f by 1.30x and 0.70x and requires both to be rejected -- the check is proved able to go red rather than assumed to be.
upgrades.no_effect: No claim row is promoted, and this time the reason is *not* the O-14 category gap -- that gap is now closed, because the measurement is of the same machine. What changed is that this project can state an error bar instead of an agreement between two of its own calculations: measured voltage constant 1.33 Vrms/Hz gives psi_f = 0.17283 Wb, our FEMM gives 0.18826 Wb, i.e. +8.93%. The rows naming ld/lq/psi_f still describe this kernel's SIL machine, which still has no geometry, so a verified 8.93% error on IPMSM_A does not become an error bar on those rows. That half of the obstruction is a decision about what the kernel's machine is, not an instrument. Recorded as F-93 (the missing external truth) and A-93 (the measurement and its band, including the admission that +-10% was chosen after the number was seen). The judgement that follows is that further FEMM depth now has low marginal value: the residual is dominated by end-leakage-free 2D, a reconstructed geometry, an assumed M400-50A B-H and the vendor Hc-derived Br, none of which a finer mesh or more rotor positions can reach.

upgrades.capability: Two things at once: a sensitivity table whose entries are the error bars this project measured elsewhere rather than numbers chosen to make the table look reasonable, and a torque witness that never forms a d-q quantity and never uses kt -- plus, in the same table, a measurement of how far that witness cannot reach.
upgrades.source: Measured bars: +8.93 % on psi_f against the ORNL bench data (A-93) and -13.4 %/-8.1 % on Ld/Lq between a 50-100 A nameplate and a 200 A point (A-92). Witness: `AbcPlant`, driven to six operating points with the inverse-Park of the d-q prediction and read back through its co-energy torque. `test_torque_map.cpp`, three new cases, one of which is a falsifier that must reject a 10 % gain error.

upgrades.capability: A second estimator for the same quantity, implemented rather than described. The header had asserted for two versions that a plain DFT bin would be biased where this fit is not; writing the bin down is what turned that sentence into a number, and the number narrowed the sentence.
upgrades.source: `test_bode_sweep.cpp`, four new cases: whole-cycle exactness for both estimators; a six-point window table at 2.00/2.50/3.00/3.20/3.40/3.50 cycles; an eight-point frequency-offset table checked against the analytic envelope `abs(sinc(dw*T/2))`; and a DC-offset case with the same projection minus its constant column as the falsifier.

upgrades.capability: A second solution of the same model, obtained by calculus instead of by stepping, plus the effect sizes of the wrong models the module is most likely to meet in service. Together they turn 'the protection trips' into 'the protection trips at this instant, and here is what a 10 % sensor error does to that instant'.
upgrades.source: `test_protection.cpp`, three new cases: the I2t trip instant from the stepping loop against `tau*ln(1/(1-limit/(i^2*tau)))` at 3.2/3.5/3.8 A, with the naive `budget/i^2` kept as the thing the measurement must not be confusable with; a sensitivity table over a +-10 % current-sense gain and a +-10 % error in the loop period; and the derating ramp against a +-10 K temperature-sensor offset.

upgrades.capability: The tracker's own input error, as a table instead of a hope. Every earlier case perturbed what the tracker was fed -- the speed, a sensor that stopped answering -- but nothing had ever moved the sensors, which is the error a real bracket actually has. `HallSetup::mount_error_rad` existed for that and had only ever been set to zero.
upgrades.source: `test_hall_decoder.cpp`, one new case sweeping a 2/4/8 degree offset on all three sensors and on one: a rigid rotation displaces the worst-case error one-for-one (maxima minus base maxima 1.988/3.976/8.002 deg, i.e. 0.994/0.994/1.000) while a single misplaced sensor carries about three quarters of it in rms (0.679/0.752/0.751) and produces a *worse* worst case (5.105 against 3.199 deg at 2 deg, reaching 1.9-2.6x the offset) -- so the bracket spec is set by the single-sensor case, which a table listing only the rigid rotation would understate by more than a factor of two. Two further cases close the tracker's remaining contract holes: a non-finite timestamp is refused without being adopted (two trackers, one fed a NaN every 37th tick, stay bit-identical) and the lower clamp is exercised on a reversal, which no forward run ever visits.

upgrades.capability: The breakaway recipe's own sensitivity, measured by separating the number the caller *tells* the sequence from the number the machine actually has -- which is the only way to ask whether the handover torque is a measurement or a setting. It is a measurement: a 50 % error in the recipe moves it by 0.0000 N*m, while the same sweep on a heavier plant moves it by 10 mN*m. Found by asking which field of the config could carry a sensitivity row and then reading the code: `breakaway_nm` appears in `validate()` and nowhere else, so the sequence is deliberately insensitive to its own brightest-sounding input.
upgrades.source: `test_stall_start.cpp`, four new cases: the release instant against `breakaway/rate` at 0.25/0.50/1.00 N*m/s (121.3 / 61.3 / 31.3 ms, so the time halves with the rate to within 2 %, while the torque moves 1 mN*m over the 4x change -- observation lag, not physics); the recipe sweep 0.015/0.030/0.045 on a 0.030 machine (0.0307 N*m at 61.3 ms, all three identical) with the heavier-plant falsifier (0.0405 N*m at 81.0 ms) that a config-driven value could not produce; the failure instant against `max/rate + give_up`, exactly 6000 ticks for a 0.2 s grace and 8001 for 0.4 s (the extra tick is the float32 accumulator, recorded not tuned away); and a step before `begin()` answering `State` with zero torque, which was the last line of the header no case had ever executed.

upgrades.capability: A second implementation of the ring contract that cannot make the defect the ring is most likely to have, driven against both rings the product uses -- which is how it came out that each *instantiation* is a separate function and the two the motors use had never dropped a sample. Plus the caller-storage channel (`SpanTrace`), which the C ABI points at and which no unit case had ever touched: a null array with a length, a real array of length zero, and a detached ring that must not write into the caller's buffer.
upgrades.source: `test_trace.cpp`, two new cases. `PlainLog` keeps every push and projects the tail -- no wrap, no head, no modulo -- and 100 pushes at capacity 8 are compared index by index against `RingTrace<8>` and `SpanTrace`, including the drop counter, the overwrite flag (which must be reported *before* the write) and the exact retained window. The detached-span case asserts `push` refuses, `at`/`latest` answer zero, `attach(nullptr, 16)` and `attach(buf, 0)` are not rings, the caller's bytes are untouched while detached, and the falsifier (real storage) does work. Coverage per instantiation, not per header: `RingTrace<8>` (the clocked motor) and `RingTrace<64>` (the traced motor) both had `++dropped_` and the out-of-range guard unexecuted.

reopened.missing: an error-source sensitivity table, and a recorder does not have one: its fidelity is exact (the sample equals the scalar reads bit for bit, and survives the text and C ABI transports bit for bit), so there is no coefficient to measure. Its only failure mode is a loss event, and that is counted exactly rather than approximately. Writing coefficients for a byte copy would fill the template rather than measure anything, which is the signal this project treats as a warning, so the row stays L2 and says so. What did close: `trace.hpp` now has zero unexecuted lines across all four instantiations (including the two the motors actually use) and `SpanTrace` -- the type the C ABI points at -- finally has a direct case.

upgrades.capability: The number a commissioning engineer actually spends when they loosen `settle_tolerance_rad`, which nothing had ever stated. The capture is a circular mean over the hold window, so a creeping rotor is captured at the arc's midpoint; the two error statistics of that sweep -- the offset bias and the circular spread -- are computable in closed form and, because they are the same arc seen twice, their ratio is a scale-free `sqrt(3)`. That ratio is what turns the tolerance into a budget for the offset instead of a knob for passing a sticky machine.
upgrades.source: `test_alignment.cpp`, two new cases. Four creep rates at a 50 ms hold: offsets 0.012475/0.024950/0.049900/0.099800 against `omega*T/2`, spreads 0.007217/0.014434/0.028869/0.057745 against `omega*T/sqrt(12)` (four digits), ratio 1.7286/1.7286/1.7285/1.7283 across an eightfold range; a still rotor captured exactly (0.000000/0.000000) as the anchor; and the derived consequence that a capture accepted at exactly the tolerance carries an offset error of `sqrt(3)*tol`. The second case executes `step()`'s `Failed` branch -- no scripted run had ever stepped past a failure -- so the rejection is shown to be sticky until `reset()`, with `handover_speed_e_rad_s` zero on every tick, which is what `Motor` reads as 'this hand-over cannot be judged'.

upgrades.capability: The sensitivity table for the step analyser, where the rows that matter are the ones that are exactly zero: the fit is invariant to the sample rate, to the window and to a DC offset because each of those is absorbed by the model, so the only error that costs anything is a target the loop does not actually reach. That turns 'the measured bandwidth is off by 9 %' into 'the measured bandwidth is off by 9 % because the C++ bench's inner loop droops, and a 5 % droop is worth 44 % of tau'.
upgrades.source: `test_step_metrics.cpp`, three new cases. Sample rate 0.2/0.5/1/2 ms at a fixed 20 ms window gives tau ratios 0.999999931/1.000000047/0.999999815/0.999999582; a 10/20/40 ms window gives 1.000000 to 0.999999; a DC offset of -1/0/+1/+5 on a 10 A step gives 1.000000. Final-value errors: 1.10/1.05/0.95/0.90 give 0.660542/0.735124/1.438404/1.767368 (asymmetric by a measured 1.65x, which falsified my first guess of 4x); noise sigma 1 %/2 % over 200 deterministic seeds gives 0.987336/0.982475 (my first bound of 'under 1:1' was also falsified -- measured 1.27:1). Settling: 18.5000 ms against `tau*ln(step/band)` = 18.4207 ms, plus the `0` and `-1` ends that no case had produced. Boundaries recorded rather than glossed: the `!(slope < 0)` guard is unreachable (every usable sample has `0 < w < 1`), and the 20-time-constant limit is float32 resolution (1.002148), not the algebra.

upgrades.capability: Which input errors an uncorrected integrator can survive and which one kills it, in numbers rather than in adjectives. The row previously said 'angle and speed on the SIL plant' and carried no measurement at all. The answer is structural: a parameter error enters as a rotating perturbation on a machine at constant speed and therefore stays bounded (with a 1/omega law that this case also records the failure point of), while a DC offset enters as the same vector every step and integrates without ever reversing.
upgrades.source: `test_back_emf_observer.cpp`, two new cases. Exact model: residue is one step of rotation, 5.2e-4 / 5.3e-3 / 1.06e-2 rad at 20 / 100 / 200 rad/s against `omega*dt` = 1e-3 / 5e-3 / 1e-2. Rs +10 %: 0.191 rad at 200 rad/s and 0.091 at 400 against `eps*Rs*iq/(omega*psi_f)` = 0.1575 / 0.0788 (1.21x / 1.16x), and 3.14 rad at 50 rad/s against the law's 0.63 -- the case asserts the saturation, so the law's domain of validity is part of the record. L +-20 %: bounded, 0.191 / 0.212 rad. DC offset 50 mA: 0.711 rad in 100 ms and 1.014 in 200, with the clean run asserted to stay under 0.02 rad so the comparison has a control. `apply_params()` -- never called by any test before -- is pinned behaviourally to the q-axis inductance (bit-identical to a `lq` build, 0.68 rad from an `ld` build), and an impossible parameter set is asserted to disable the observer rather than let it run on the old model.

upgrades.capability: The gain law's own error budget, and the asymmetry inside it: it cancels the mechanical pole exactly in continuous time, and on a sampled loop with an ideal current source it lands within 3.5 % of the request across a decade of bandwidth -- but of the two nameplate terms only the inertia moves the bandwidth, one for one. That is the number a commissioning run needs (fit J before b), and it is also what bounds how much of step_metrics' +9.15 % this row can be blamed for: none of it.
upgrades.source: `test_motor.cpp`, one new case. The -3 dB is found by bisection on the amplitude gain of the sampled loop (20 kHz, ideal current loop, torque = kt*i in the same period) at 50/100/200/400 rad/s: ratios 1.02516/1.02661/1.02948/1.03462, residual tracking `wb*dt`. Inertia error -20/20/50 %: 0.7991/1.2012/1.5044 of the clean row -- one for one. Friction error -50/+50/+200 % at a non-negligible `b = 1e-3`: coefficient 0.0537/0.0543/0.0523 per unit, 18x below inertia. The first version of the friction block scaled `b` *down* by 1e-3 and measured an exact zero, which proved only that a negligible term is negligible; that experiment was replaced rather than reported.

upgrades.capability: The homing recipe as an envelope, measured in samples rather than seconds -- and the discovery that the clock the envelope is measured against is a float32 accumulator, so a long recipe times out early and a very long one never times out at all. Its third leg is the origin itself: the zero cannot be better than where the axis was when the index was honoured, so an index delay is a distance, and that distance is paid for in creep speed.
upgrades.source: `test_homing_routine.cpp`, two new cases. Envelope: the reference is driven with the speed the routine actually commands and the index pulsed when travel crosses a known mark. 1 rad/s for 1 s at 100 us buys 0.9999 rad, exactly `(ticks - 1)*creep*dt`, so a mark at 0.9999 or 1.0 is missed and 0.9990 is found; at 10 rad/s, 9.99 found and 10.0 missed. Timer: a 512 s recipe at 40 kHz fires after 446.664 s of real time (12.8 % fast) in 17 866 579 ticks, and a 520 s recipe does not fire in 40 M ticks (1000 s of real time). The floor is `2^24*dt` rounded up to a power of two -- 512 / 2048 / 32768 s for dt = 25 us / 100 us / 1 ms -- checked both through the routine (no finish past the floor) and on a bare float mirroring `elapsed_s_ += dt_s`. The fix (tick counting, or a double accumulator) is a library change this row does not make; the case is written to fail if the behaviour changes. Origin: the same sweep, with the pulse delayed 0/1/5/20 ticks after the crossing and the travel at the honouring tick compared against the true mark -- 1.00/2.00/6.00/21.00 samples at 1 rad/s, exactly `(jitter + 1)*creep*dt`, and the ratio to `creep*dt` stays 21.000 at 0.5/1/2/4 rad/s, so the error is one-for-one in creep speed while the search time is one-over-creep speed: `error x time` is fixed.

upgrades.capability: A clock with a stated law, in place of five unstated ones. `core::ElapsedClock` counts nanoseconds in a uint64 and is exact to 1 ns; the four routines that own a timeout now use it, and the rule that produced them -- a duration that only grows is not a float -- is enforced by `gates.py clocks` rather than by memory.
upgrades.source: `test_elapsed_clock.cpp`, two cases, plus the rewritten homing timeout case. The discriminator is a second implementation of the same sum: 20 480 000 periods of 25 us reach 512 s on tick 20 480 000 in the clock and on tick 17 866 579 in float (446.664 s of real time, 12.8 % fast, and frozen from there). The same three homing recipes now fire at 40 000 / 20 480 000 / 20 800 000 ticks; before the fix the 512 s recipe fired at 17 866 579 and the 520 s one never fired at all (40 M ticks, 1000 s of real time). `gates.py clocks` scans include/ and src/ for a float accumulated with a dt term and fails on every one that is not on an allow list carrying its bound; its selftest classifies four snippets so a classifier that finds nothing cannot pass. Measured while doing it: the conversion `seconds * 1e9F` in one float multiply needs 39 bits and left a 520 s recipe 16 us long, one tick late -- split into whole seconds and a fraction.

upgrades.capability: The reference itself, verified to be one: zero lag, independence from every electrical input including NaN and infinities, and reset to zeros -- with a real observer as the falsifier, so the case cannot pass on a class that ignores its inputs for the wrong reason.
upgrades.source: `test_ideal_observer.cpp`, one new case. Four hostile inputs (NaN pairs, infinities, a 1e9 V command with a zero period, a negative period) leave the reported truth bit-identical at 2.5 rad / -1400 rad/s; the truth set this period is reported this period; and `BackEmfObserver` on the same two opposite voltages answers differently, which is what makes the independence assertion a discriminator rather than a tautology.

reopened.missing: an error-source sensitivity, which cannot exist here: the class has no model to be wrong with -- it reports the plant truth by construction, and that absence is the whole reason it is the reference. L2 is the terminal level for this row, and the measurable substitute (that it stays a cheat channel: zero lag, input-independent, reset to zeros) is now pinned. Anything further would be measuring a model this class does not have.

upgrades.capability: The two-fault ranking, derived from how long each detector takes to assert instead of from the enum it is written in -- and the exact place where that derivation runs out, stated as a limit rather than filled with a borrowed severity order.
upgrades.source: `test_protection.cpp`, one new case. Every threshold code asserts after one step at a 1 % overshoot (OverCurrent, OverVoltage, UnderVoltage, OverTemperature), so the machine supplies no order among them; I2t asserts after 13 269 steps (0.663 s) and Stall after 10 000 (0.500 s), so the physics supplies exactly one statement -- thresholds before durations -- and the enum is a linear extension of it. Path independence is measured over all five physically possible threshold pairs in both onset orders: the code and the mask agree (0x006, 0x00a, 0x012, 0x014, 0x018), the winner is the lower-ranked and not the first to arrive. The first version of the pair block applied the second fault's whole input row over the first, un-violating it, and made the library look order-dependent; the union construction is what fixed it.

upgrades.capability: The field-weakening go/no-go run as a selection function over the machines this project actually has parameters for, plus the regime map of the ellipse sensitivity -- and, on the way, the discovery that the rule the header advertised could never be the one that decided.
upgrades.source: `test_field_weakening.cpp`, three new cases. Selection: five rows (SIL machine, a published SPMSM-class drive, a published IPM raw and Ld/Lq-corrected, the 2004 Prius traction motor) with the health check rejecting the row whose own table has Lq<Ld; no accepted machine passes; lambdas 0.115/0.235/0.252/0.253 against a line at 1.0. Rule: the verdict is `i_char <= i_max`, bisected to 1e-5; the old `ratio<0.6 && speed_gain>=1.5` expression is unreachable-as-true because the ratio half implies λ>5/3 which the early branch already accepted -- F-107, fixed in the header rather than pinned as-is. Sensitivity: psi_f +/-10% and Rs +/-20% at 2910/3200/3500/3800 rad/s; the point is on the current circle at all four (`|i| = i_max`), the law is an upper bound (0.67/0.50/0.24/0.01 of it upward), and the two directions differ by 1.31x growing to 30.3x.

upgrades.capability: The PI closed on a plant, measured against two models at once: the exact droop law it has with no free parameter, and the continuum it is a sampling of -- which is how the textbook pole-only overshoot formula turned out to be wrong for this structure.
upgrades.source: `test_pi.cpp`, three new cases. Droop: three disturbance levels at kp = 0.01 give 0.100000 / 0.200000 / 0.500000 against d/kp exactly, and 1e-6 with ki = 1. Continuum: the closed loop is (kp*s + ki)/(J*s^2 + kp*s + ki) with a zero at -ki/kp, so the pole-only law's 16.3 % / 0 % are 29.8 % / 13.5 % in the loop; the same loop as two ODEs at 10 ns agrees to 0.06 / 0.04 / 0.02 % at kp = 0.01/0.02/0.03. Period error: the controller's own dt is what scales the integral, so a k-times-wrong period moves the time to first peak as 1/sqrt(k) -- measured 1.0415 / 1.0166 / 0.9793 / 0.9627 against 1.0541 / 1.0260 / 0.9759 / 0.9535.

upgrades.capability: The filters measured against their own z-domain transfer function by sweep, and the one number a user actually needs -- where the corner really is, as a function of the sampling ratio -- which turns out to be the opposite side of the request from the obvious guess.
upgrades.source: `test_filters.cpp`, four new cases. Corner: bisected on |H(e^{jw})| of the recurrence at five fc*dt ratios, 0.9847 / 0.9305 / 0.8751 / 0.7918 / 0.6518 x the request, monotone in fc*dt and asserted as such. Sweep: sine in, both command and response fit by `sinusoid_fit.hpp`, quotient vs the analytic model to 0.000 % and 0.0001 rad at seven frequencies; corner phase -0.7051 vs the analogue -0.7854. Period error: corner ratio 0.9105 / 0.9555 / 1.0441 / 1.0877 for k = 0.90/0.95/1.05/1.10. Moving average: null at fs/N = 3.1e-17, group delay 3.5000 samples from the phase slope, Dirichlet kernel magnitude 0.90176 both ways.

upgrades.capability: The modulator's linear range as the hexagon it actually is, with the boundary matched to the geometry at six angles, plus the two identities a control loop relies on: the mapping has no gain error, and a wrong bus voltage comes out exactly and inverted.
upgrades.source: `test_svpwm.cpp`, four new cases. Boundary: bisected on the code at 0/10/20/30/40/50 degrees, 16.00000 V at a vertex and 13.85641 V at a flat side, matching (2/3*v_bus)*cos(30)/cos(theta'-30) to 1e-5 relative. Full-turn sweep: 0 of 72 saturated at 0.999x the inscribed circle, 6 at the circle itself, 66 of 72 at 2/3*v_bus. Reconstruction: duties -> (duty-mean)*v_bus -> Clarke equals the request to <=1e-6 V at seven angles in all sectors. Sensitivity: realised/commanded = 1/k, measured 1.111111 / 1.052632 / 0.952381 / 0.909091 for k = 0.90/0.95/1.05/1.10.

upgrades.capability: The mode machine measured as a graph instead of as a table: reachability from Idle, Fault as the only sink, and the refusal measured as an exact zero on state and +1 on the counter -- which is what makes an existing diagnostic counter trustworthy.
upgrades.source: `test_sm.cpp`, three new cases. Relation measured on the code over 4 start states x 4 targets: 7 legal edges, out-degree 2/3/2/0, in-degree 2/1/1/3, all four states reachable from Idle by BFS, Fault out-degree 0. Refusals: 9 of 16 cells refuse and each leaves the state unchanged with the counter +1 exactly, plus 8 out-of-range targets (static_cast<MotorState>(4) and (200)) equally inert. Retry: request(current) refused three times -> counter +3, state unchanged. Found and fixed: the class docstring described `Idle -> Align -> Run` and stopped, omitting the two abort edges back to Idle -- F-108.

upgrades.capability: The rate limiter measured as an exact step count instead of as a waveform: the number of steps a ramp needs is a ceiling, it is exact to the step, and both factors enter it one-for-one -- so a ramp schedule can be sized from the nameplate with a proportional error and no leverage.
upgrades.source: `test_limits.cpp`, three new cases. 14 (rate, period) combinations, all powers of two so the arithmetic is exact: `steps = ceil(travel/(rate*dt))` holds as an equality (32/16/8 steps for budgets 1/32, 1/16, 1/8), and the point with a budget of 2.0 for a travel of 1.0 reaches the target in one step and lands on it. Boundary side of the `min`: inside the budget the output is the target on the same call, exactly at the budget it lands on the target, one step beyond is one budget, and a non-positive period changes nothing.

upgrades.capability: The map's between-row error measured against its own law: it is the chord error, it goes as the square of the spacing, it reads low, and the spacing rather than the row count is the lever that sizes a table.
upgrades.source: `test_machine_map.cpp`, one new case. Analytic saturation L0/(1+(i/ik)^2), L0=4e-4 H, ik=120 A, 60 A held as a chord centre at every spacing. Measured interpolation error 1.538e-6 / 3.630e-7 / 8.936e-8 H at spacings 40 / 20 / 10 A against the chord law 1.422e-6 / 3.556e-7 / 8.889e-8: ratios 1.082 / 1.021 / 1.005, halving ratio 4.062 against the law's 4.0. Sign checked (the chord lies below a concave curve, so the table reads low).

upgrades.capability: The document's number width is justified by measurement rather than by taste: `%.9g` is FLT_DECIMAL_DIG, the shortest width that round-trips every float, and `%.8g` is measured failing.
upgrades.source: `test_machine_map_text.cpp`, one new case. 4000 deterministic samples (LCG) drawn from the map's own range, each written and read through the library's own codec and compared on the bits: `%.9g` 4000/4000, `%.8g` 3993/4000 -- the last bit is lost on 7 of 4000, so the falsifier for a narrower width exists and fires.

upgrades.capability: The C8 capability piece the plan still listed as missing: an observer that carries BOTH inductances, so the d-axis current that MtpaReference is defined by no longer costs steering accuracy. The saliency term the single-L model discards is a closed-form bias, and it is removed exactly rather than reduced.
upgrades.source: `test_dual_inductance_observer.cpp`, five cases. Algebra: the flux relation is a quadratic in `x = e^(j*theta)`; seeded with the flux a salient machine has at a known angle and handed `v = Rs*i`, the inversion returns the angle to 4.768e-07 rad over 48 (angle, i_d, i_q) combinations, and on Ld == Lq it is bit-identical to the shipped observer's `arg(psi - L*i)` (gap 0.000e+00 over 36 combinations). Model: on the repository's speed-locked plant with the exact steady-state d-q voltage, the single-L bias is `atan((ld-lq)*i_d/psi_f)` -- measured 0.0273/0.0433/0.0604/0.0773/0.0939 rad against the law's 0.0210/0.0420/0.0629/0.0838/0.1046 (within 30 %), monotone in i_d and independent of speed -- while the dual-L answer is flat at 0.0145 to 0.0157 rad over the same range and 6.5x better at 2.5 A. Documented floor: a backward-Euler flux integrator lags by about w_e*dt/2 (0.0025 rad at 100 rad/s, 0.02 at 800), so the table is taken at 100 rad/s and the faster numbers are recorded as unusable. The combinations matrix gains `MtpaReference + DualInductanceObserver -> allow` and a wildcard allow, both pointing at this file.
upgrades.no_effect: Not wired into `SwitchableObserver` yet, so no C caller can select it: the header and its measurements exist, the runtime selector and the ABI are the next batch. `core/observer/switchable_observer.hpp` stays at L1 for that reason and not because its forwarding is untested.

upgrades.capability: The dual-inductance observer is reachable at run time and through C: a fifth selector member, a new `foc_observer_t` value, and a hand-over that can carry the current as well as the angle -- so an MTPA drive can be handed to the observer that tolerates its `i_d`.
upgrades.source: `test_switchable_observer.cpp` and `test_api_observer_selector.cpp`, one case each, plus `test_dual_inductance_observer.cpp`'s `seed_at` case. Hand-over A/B into the new member: the angle-only seed and the angle-plus-current seed end 0.005330 rad apart after 50 steps at 0.1 A, and a pure integrator never forgets, so that gap is permanent -- which is why `hand_over_to(kind, i_ab)` exists and why the one-argument form is not enough for the only member whose state is the stator flux. `seed_at` is checked by seeding from an angle and a current and then handing `v = Rs*i`, which leaves the flux where it is: the answer is that angle to 1e-3 rad at every current, while the current's own flux is worth more than 0.02 rad of offset at 2.5 A. Two defects flushed out by wiring it: `foc_motor_set_observer` refused the new mode because its upper bound was a second copy of the enumeration (`FOC_OBSERVER_BLENDED`), and `foc_types.h`'s Chinese note still claimed HFI and BLENDED answer `FOC_ERR_NOT_IMPL` while the English note above it said all four were wired.

reopened.missing: no case hands over *out of* the blend while its band is active, which is the one path where the outgoing estimate comes from a composite rather than a single observer.

upgrades.capability: A negative result recorded instead of a column that flatters: the observer screening table cannot separate the dual-inductance observer from the single-L one, because at this flux linkage the inverter's dead time is the same size as the model difference. What the table can and cannot see is now stated.
upgrades.source: `test_observer_screening.cpp`, one new case. `Lq/Ld = 2.5`, 800 rad/s, `iq = 0.5 A`: at `i_d` = 0 / -0.5 / -1 / -2 A the single-L observer reads 0.0253 / 0.0678 / 0.1240 / 0.1708 rad and the dual-inductance one 0.0197 / 0.0579 / 0.1217 / 0.1699, i.e. the same number to 2 % where the models differ by 0.105 rad (the bias law of `test_dual_inductance_observer.cpp`). The assertion is written both ways: both stay outside the 0.15 rad ceiling at 2 A, and the two must not separate -- if they ever do, the instrument changed and the table has to be retaken.
upgrades.no_effect: The screening table's existing columns are unchanged; this adds what it cannot resolve, not a new verdict about the observers. `MtpaReference x DualInductanceObserver` remains `allow` on the plant measurement, not on this rig.
